frontier.hypothesis: A cse basic-block boundary can be placed between `eda`'s definition and the `qf & 0x30` block WITHOUT relocating `magic = 0x80190800` out of the prologue, closing region A for less than the 11 the if/ELSE form costs.
frontier.mechanism: cse_end_of_basic_block (cse.c:8039-8184) ends a block at any CODE_LABEL it cannot AROUND-extend past. The if/ELSE barrier is only ONE such condition; the extension is also refused when LABEL_NUSES (JUMP_LABEL (p)) != 1 -- i.e. a join label targeted by TWO jumps, which is exactly what a short-circuit `&&` / `||` condition emits -- and the extended block is additionally capped by PATH_SIZE followed jumps.
frontier.next_probe: Read cse.c:8039-8184 and enumerate every block-ending / extension-refusing condition. For each, find whether any statement in target insns 3..54 is byte-consistent with a spelling that produces it (a two-branch compound condition is the prime candidate). Screen each candidate in the mini TU first (tmp/grind/func_8003B9D0/s3/, ~2 seconds per variant, look for `1100($reg)` instead of `%lo(D_80101EDA+1100)`), and only then port it to src and sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining ~4 points of the closing form (the `la` at mine[38..39] instead of target's tgt[55..56]) close if the boundary sits late enough that `eda`'s assignment can also sit late -- immediately before the `qf & 0x30` test.
frontier.mechanism: cc1 emits the pointer's set where the C statement is, and the first scheduler then drops it into the nearest load-delay slot; the assignment must precede the boundary, so the boundary's position directly bounds the `la`'s position.
frontier.next_probe: For every boundary form F1 turns up, run the session-1 normalized diff (tmp/grind/func_8003B9D0/s1/diff.py) and read the `la` position BEFORE judging the score -- prefer the form whose boundary is latest. Note the two regions are independent (session-2 K7), so region A can be evaluated on its own.

frontier.hypothesis: func_8003AFFC takes the D_800A3878 object pointer as an argument, and our zero-argument call is a decompilation error rather than a codegen choice.
frontier.mechanism: m2c infers the signature from $a0 being live and unreloaded across the call (tgt[48] sets it, tgt[68] is the jal); a genuine void-argument callee would not require that liveness.
frontier.next_probe: Read asm/funcs/func_8003AFFC.s to see whether it actually consumes $a0. If it does, correct the prototype and the call site (src/code6cac_c2.c carries three duplicate `extern void func_8003AFFC(void);` declarations, at lines 73, 74 and 171, which should be reconciled to one) and re-measure. Expect byte-neutrality; the value is correctness of the decompilation and of func_8003AFFC's own future grind.
